name: Mortar for Bricks Builder
author: Samir Haddad

sections.description:
Mortar adds practical workflow tools to Bricks Builder: manage BEM classes, test responsive layouts, write CSS faster and work directly from the structure panel.

Each tool is explained in the Mortar settings panel with a description and a live example, so you can choose what fits your workflow.

Included modules

  • BEM Generator: create and rename BEM classes in bulk. Review the element hierarchy and proposed changes before applying, with nested block detection and protected component instances. Your default All/None selection is saved per user across browsers.
  • Viewport Resizer: test responsive layouts with a canvas-width slider, breakpoint markers and a reset control. Use Bricks’ native width field for precise values.
  • CSS Recipes: create, edit and manage reusable CSS shortcuts. Customize, disable or restore the included recipes, with changes shared across your site.
  • Smart Values: convert CSS variables, calculations and pixel-to-rem values as you type, including in the Custom CSS editor.
  • HTML Tags: change semantic HTML tags directly from the structure panel, including when editing component definitions.
  • Style Indicators: see which elements have styles applied through classes or element IDs.
  • Sidebar Shortcuts: add frequently used elements through a configurable quick-insert rail.
  • Auto-Select Class: automatically select an element’s first existing, unlocked global class. Bricks 2.4 also provides a native first-class option.
  • Export ID Styles to Class: move ID-level styles to the first CSS class in one click.
  • Expand Children: expand or collapse an entire subtree at once, including inside component definitions.
  • Editor Theme: customise the builder’s accent and surface colours with presets and saved palettes. The Custom CSS editor follows your theme too.

Requirements

Mortar requires Bricks Builder and runs inside its editor.

Independence and trademark

Mortar is an independent project, not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by Bricks Builder or its makers. “Bricks” is a trademark of its respective owner and is used here only to describe compatibility.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin ZIP via Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin, or copy the mortar folder to wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Activate Mortar through the Plugins screen.
  3. Open the Bricks Builder editor — a Mortar icon appears in the top toolbar.
  4. Click it to open the settings panel and enable the modules you want.
sections.faq:
Does it require Bricks Builder?

Yes. Mortar runs only inside the Bricks Builder editor (tested with Bricks 2.x, up to 2.4).

Where are the settings?

Inside the Bricks editor, click the Mortar icon in the top toolbar. The panel lists every module with a description and an example.

Can I turn modules off?

Yes. Every module has its own toggle; save and reload to apply.

How do updates work?

Through the WordPress Plugins screen, like any other plugin from the directory.
sections.changelog:
1.9.0

  • New: CSS Recipes manager to create, edit, duplicate, delete and individually enable or disable custom recipes shared across your site. Included recipes can be customized and restored. Access it directly from the Custom CSS toolbar and return with your text and cursor preserved.
  • Improved: More consistent module settings, clearer access to CSS Recipes and a more compact Editor Theme.
  • Fixed: Export ID Styles to Class now replaces the element ID with %root% in Custom CSS, including responsive styles and pseudo states.

1.8.0

  • New: Per-user BEM default selection (All/None), shared across browsers.
  • Improved: BEM panel with element hierarchy, change previews and adaptive sizing.
  • Improved: Nested BEM block detection and protection of component instances.
  • Fixed: BEM class renaming, modifiers and undo/redo.
  • Fixed: BEM, HTML Tags and Expand Children support inside component definitions.
  • Fixed: Saved BEM preferences are removed when uninstalling the plugin.

1.7.3

BEM Generator now preserves element settings when copying ID styles to a class.

  • Fixed: “Copy ID styles to Class” moves only CSS settings, so button styles and form fields remain on their elements.
  • Fixed: Custom CSS generated by Bricks CSS Sync moves from the element ID selector to the BEM class instead of leaving duplicate ID and class declarations.

1.7.2

Viewport Resizer is easier to read and use in narrow builder windows.

  • Fixed: breakpoint width labels no longer overlap when the builder workspace is narrow.
  • Improved: a slimmer slider, clearer width markers and reset control, and a new panel icon for showing and hiding it. Exact widths use Bricks’ native W field.
  • New: Auto-Select Class and Sidebar Shortcuts show a Legacy badge on Bricks 2.4+, with notes explaining the related native features and the differences that remain.

1.7.1

Viewport Resizer now follows the available canvas space and stays out of the way until you need it.

  • Fixed: Viewport Resizer no longer stops at 2000px. Its maximum width now adapts to the usable preview area and the current canvas scale, while preserving the active width and configured breakpoint defaults.
  • Fixed: Viewport Resizer starts hidden until you open it from the breakpoint toolbar, unless you have explicitly chosen to leave it open.
  • Fixed: the Viewport Resizer toolbar button now uses the same restrained interaction as Bricks controls: no coloured background, with a purple icon on hover and when active.

1.7.0

Viewport Resizer adds precise responsive-width testing directly inside the Bricks builder.

  • New: Viewport Resizer adds a responsive-width slider below Bricks’ native breakpoints: drag to test widths, use Bricks’ W field for exact input, see the device lanes and configured default widths, restore the active breakpoint, and show or hide it from the breakpoint toolbar. Mortar remembers the choice for the next builder session.
  • Fixed: Sidebar Shortcuts now stays visible while scrolling a long structure tree, and its icons remain readable with light Bricks themes.

1.6.4

Compatible with Bricks 2.4. Required if you are updating Bricks.

  • Fixed: on Bricks 2.4 the icon that opens the Mortar panel was not there at all, leaving no way to reach the settings. Bricks replaced its single toolbar with one toolbar per position, and Mortar was still looking for the old one.
  • Fixed: the icon now comes back on its own when Bricks rebuilds the toolbar, which 2.4 does every time you move it or open the interface customiser.
  • New: if the interface customiser is used to empty the toolbar completely, Bricks removes it from the editor. Mortar then falls back to a floating button, so the panel is never out of reach.
  • Fixed: moving the Bricks panel or the structure to another dock left every new row without its BEM button, HTML tag, style indicator and shortcut rail until the editor was reloaded.
  • Fixed: Editor Theme tinted the toolbar logo through a selector 2.4 no longer has. Press Apply once to pick it up.

1.6.3

BEM Generator: the classes you apply now stay applied after saving. Updating is recommended.

  • Fixed: after applying classes and reloading the editor, some elements came back without their class, even though the class itself was still there in the project. It hit the elements that had no styles of their own yet, which is why it looked random.
  • Fixed: a whole run of the generator could be lost on save when the last thing you clicked was the canvas rather than the panel.
  • Fixed: the classes you just applied now show their styles in the canvas straight away, instead of only after reloading the editor.
  • Fixed: “Create new & delete old” now really deletes. The old class used to come back on the next save.
  • Fixed: Export ID Styles to Class could lose the export the same way, leaving the styles on the element and on the class at once.

1.6.2

CSS Recipes now expand in the editor you are typing in, not just the first one on screen.

  • Fixed: recipes stopped expanding when more than one code editor was open at once, for example an element’s Custom CSS and a Code element. Only the first editor on the page worked and the others failed silently.
  • Fixed: undo now takes back just the recipe you expanded, instead of the whole field.

1.6.1

Styles applied from Mortar now show up in the canvas straight away.

  • Fixed: CSS Recipes and Smart Values put the value in the panel, but the canvas kept showing the old style until you saved and reloaded the editor. It happened when you picked the element in the canvas and went straight to the field.

1.6.0

BEM Generator: renaming works again, and it now works the way renaming should. Updating is recommended.

  • Fixed: the generator was adding “–element” to the end of every class it created. Nobody asked for it. An empty modifier field was being read as the word “element”.
  • Fixed: renaming did not rename. It created a new class with no styles and left the old one on the element. Same cause as the above, which also forced every run into “keep old classes”.
  • Changed: renaming a class now renames it wherever it is used, which is what renaming means. Its styles, its custom CSS and every element using it come along. If you want a new class for this element only and the rest left alone, use “Create new & remove old”.
  • New: the class field starts from the class the element already has, instead of a name guessed from its label. Renaming is now editing what you see.
  • New: “Create new & delete old” asks before it runs. It deletes classes from the whole project, so the button now says what is about to happen and needs a second click.
  • Fixed: deleting classes left other elements pointing at a class that no longer existed. Those leftovers could later reappear as an unrelated class.
  • Fixed: renaming to a name that already exists no longer leaves two classes sharing the same name.
  • Fixed: custom CSS written inside a class is now rewritten by Bricks itself when the class is renamed or copied, so its selectors keep matching.

1.5.0

Mostly bug fixes, a few of them data loss. Updating is recommended.

  • BEM Generator: running it twice on the same block no longer leaves elements without their class.
  • BEM Generator: renaming no longer deletes classes that other parts of the site were using.
  • BEM Generator: “Copy ID styles to Class” no longer strips content, loops and conditions from the element, and it keeps the classes it already had.
  • BEM Generator: modifiers with spaces or symbols now become valid class names.
  • BEM Generator: elements inside components are found again.
  • Export ID Styles to Class: no longer moves content into the class. Accordion items and form fields could be lost.
  • Export ID Styles to Class: exports to the class whose menu you opened, not always the first one.
  • Mortar’s buttons now always show up in the structure tree.
  • Editor Theme: your own builder CSS is no longer overwritten, and it comes back when you turn the theme off.
  • Editor Theme: a save that fails is now reported instead of showing success.
  • Sidebar Shortcuts: the rail hides together with the structure panel.
  • Expand Children: expanding a large branch no longer closes branches that were already open.
  • The builder feels lighter: the plugin was loading twice.
  • Deleting the plugin now restores the Bricks editor theme and cleans up after itself.

1.4.0

  • Smart Values: type a pixel value with the “cte” suffix and press Enter to convert it to em, for example 20cte becomes 1.25em. This joins the existing “ctr” shortcut for rem.
  • Smart Values now works in the Custom CSS code editor too. Type a value and press the semicolon key to expand it: –primary becomes var(–primary), a math expression is wrapped in calc(…), and 20ctr or 20cte convert to rem or em.

1.3.0

  • Smart Values: type a pixel value with the “ctr” suffix and press Enter to convert it to rem, for example 20ctr becomes 1.25rem. Works in element fields and in the Custom CSS code editor.
  • Editor Theme: the Custom CSS code editor now follows your theme, with a dark, readable colour scheme. Optional overrides let you set the editor background and syntax accent.
  • Expand Children: fixed a bug where expanding an element could jump the selection to one of its children. It now keeps your current selection.

1.2.1

  • Fixed: on sites updating from an earlier version, the Editor Theme module could open an empty panel. It now enables and opens correctly on existing installs.

1.2.0

  • New module: Editor Theme. Colour the Bricks builder to match your brand. Pick your accent and surface colours and the whole editor follows, with presets, your own saved palettes, and one-click apply.
  • Fixed a bug where the settings panel could get stuck when dragged quickly across the canvas.

1.1.2

  • Style indicators: more accurate (they no longer light up for elements without real CSS styling) and they now refresh instantly when you add or remove a class.
  • Auto-select class: faster and lighter when moving between elements.

1.1.1

  • Performance: lighter, more stable editor during long sessions, with less background work and no slow memory build-up.

1.1.0

  • Sidebar Shortcuts: manage the rail right in the editor. The new “+” button opens a popup to add, remove and reorder shortcuts, and changes save automatically.
  • HTML Tags: fixed a bug and improved element-tag detection, so the correct tag now shows reliably on more elements, including Button and Image.
  • Accessibility: keyboard support to add, remove and reorder shortcuts in the popup.

1.0.0

  • First public release on WordPress.org.
  • Settings panel (master–detail) with a description and live example per module.
  • Modules: BEM Generator, Style Indicators, Sidebar Shortcuts, HTML Tags, Auto-Select Class, Export ID Styles to Class, CSS Recipes, Expand Children and Smart Values.
  • Accessibility: visible focus rings, ARIA labels and keyboard activation.
